messages:
Claire (People Ops): quick question — an IC asked if they can bump their 401(k) deferral from 6% to 10% mid-year and have the extra withheld while they're going on unpaid parental leave next month. any special steps?

Raj (Payroll): short answer: yes you can change elections going forward, but contributions stop during unpaid leave unless they opt for an ACH to the plan admin. payroll needs the election by the cutoff to be effective. next cutoff is 2026-05-15 for a 6/1 effective date. :calendar:

Ben (Eng): @Claire ok if they submit after the cutoff can we do a retro adjustment to withhold the difference for previous pay periods?

Maya (Benefits Vendor): hi all — vendor note: we cannot retroactively withhold funds for past payroll periods. if employee misses the payroll file, options are: 1) make a manual trustee-to-trustee deposit (one-time employee contribution) — requires our one-time deposit form and proof of payroll election, or 2) wait until next payroll cycle. Manual deposits must be processed within plan limits for annual deferral/catch-up. link: https://hr.redwood.com/forms/one-time-deposit.pdf

Raj (Payroll): adding process details: to change deferral we need an updated 401k election PDF or the self-service portal confirmation by cutoff. please include new pre-tax% and any Roth split. for catch-up (50+) also indicate catch-up amount. sample fields we need:
```
Employee ID: 12345
Effective date: 2026-06-01
Pre-tax deferral: 10%
Roth deferral: 0%
Catch-up deferral: $1,000
```

Claire (People Ops): and about the unpaid parental leave — will the employer match continue while they’re on unpaid leave? does vesting change?

Maya (Benefits Vendor): match: match follows contributions. if there are no employee deferrals during unpaid leave, there is nothing to match. some companies choose to make a discretionary employer contribution during approved leave — that's a company policy decision, not handled by the vendor automatically. vesting schedule is unchanged — vesting is based on service/tenure, not contribution activity.

Ben (Eng): if they want to maintain savings while on leave, what's the simplest path?

Raj (Payroll): easiest: submit the higher deferral before cutoff so more is taken on the last paid paycheck(s) before leave. alternative: employee can do the trustee deposit via vendor, but it's more paperwork. i can DM the employee the portal link and cutoff calendar.

Claire (People Ops): thanks — i'll message them. one more: do we need manager approval for the election change?

Maya (Benefits Vendor): no manager approval required for deferral changes. just employee election + payroll processing.

Payroll Bot: payroll file for 2026-05 processed and sent to benefits vendor (file id: pf_202605). :white_check_mark:

Claire (People Ops): perfect — closing this thread. i'll post the how-to in the handbook with the cutoff dates and the vendor one-time deposit link. :memo:
